title: Identifiability of Noise Sources in Bodily Judgments
subtitle: A computational audit of parietal stimulation and a conditional paired-readout design
author: Hongju Liu
decision_scope: A substantive scientific and editorial judgment after internal AI-assisted reviews; not external peer review, acceptance, author approval or a DOI-backed preprint release.
revision_relation: Deepens the unpublished CTD v0.1 paper; preserves v0.1 in its separate record. Does not amend the published SCU preprint.

net_contribution.claim: The released information-criterion rows match a second negation of positive NLL. The corrected aggregate still favors Sigma.
A conditional signed-SOA symmetry diagnostic rejects the centered independent-binomial family without fitting its parameters.
A corrected fixed within-cell five-fold comparison favors Sigma plus task-specific centers over Prior plus task-specific centers, conditional on these retrospective families.
An explicit fixed-sensory, variable-criterion implementation preserves all 1,260 source marginal probabilities while retaining the source threshold policy.

One additional population joint probability identifies shared Gaussian variance under calibrated centers and independent criteria/lapses; bounded criterion correlation yields a sharp set and central weak identification is quantified.

inherited_material: Gaussian addition of independent variances and sensory/criterion ambiguity (including Yarrow et al.).
Bias and decision strategy in simultaneity judgments (Cabrera et al.; Yarrow et al.).
BCI accounts of ownership and sensory uncertainty (Chancel et al.; D’Angelo et al.).
Bivariate normal derivative identities (Plackett) and the general principle that extra measurements can aid noise identification.
The SCU distinction between matching behavior and verified source use; CTD v0.1 descriptive width results.
priority_status: No universal first-discovery claim. The exact combined audit and bounded paired-readout result are proposed contributions; exhaustive priority is not established.

seven_questions.precise_problem: When does evidence for a condition-dependent response width identify a sensory source rather than an observationally equivalent decision implementation?
seven_questions.citable_increment: Concrete auditable arithmetic correction, response-family failure, final refit comparison, exact source-calibrated twin and conditional joint measurement boundary.
seven_questions.nearest_prior_art: literature/V02_NOVELTY_AND_PUBLICATION_AUDIT.md and manuscript Section 8 explicitly credit the closest sources and qualify priority.
seven_questions.testable_scope: Finite released response cells; declared independent-binomial and Gaussian models. Proofs state same-sample, center, threshold, independence and lapse premises; actual human realization remains open.
seven_questions.reproduction: Three unchanged workbooks, original model-code snapshot, full saved fits/partitions, exact mathematical checks, independent likelihood audits, superseded failures and all repairs are retained.
seven_questions.future_reuse: A researcher can audit a fitted response family, construct an equivalent implementation, then check whether a proposed joint measurement actually separates the relevant source hypotheses under independently justified exclusions.
seven_questions.position_and_preservation: One revised methods and secondary-analysis paper with English manuscript and Chinese handoff; CTD2 stays a disabled map candidate. Persistence is recorded separately after successful readback.

not_established: A sensory locus of the stimulation effect
A directly measured experience or UCT-specific prediction
External peer review or journal acceptance
next_empirical_question: Can one build and independently calibrate two readouts of the same internal sample, with criterion-dependence and correlated lapses bounded independently, before using the proposed inverse?
parallel_main_line_preserved: A3M selected bodily/action familiarity H and its physically credible R≠L manipulation remain a separate open objective.
